name: Add Claro Media Library to Theme
description: Injects Claro's media library templates, preprocess callbacks and CSS into the active theme's registry so the media library renders with its full Claro styling even when it is opened outside the admin theme.
project_description: Despite its name and 'Theme' package this is a module (type: module), not a theme. Drupal's media library modal, its Twig templates and its preprocessing live in the Claro admin theme. When the library is opened from something rendered in the front-end (or any non-Claro) theme, those theme hooks are absent from the active theme's registry, so the grid collapses into an unstyled list and the add form loses its layout. This module implements hook_theme_registry_alter() to register Claro's media-library theme hooks (media, media--media-library, media_library_wrapper, media_library_item and its --small / --widget variants, the media_library views templates, fieldset--media-library-widget, links--media-library-menu, the add-form item_list/details/container hooks) pointing at Claro's own template files, then a force step that array_replaces existing core hooks so they use Claro's templates and preprocess chains. It also implements hook_library_info_alter() to append its own small compatibility CSS library to the media_library widget/view/ui libraries, and form/views hooks (hook_form_alter, three hook_form_FORM_ID_alter for the add/upload/oembed forms, hook_views_pre_render) that manually invoke Claro's own alter and preprocess logic. Each delegating callback tries the legacy procedural claro.theme function first (e.g. claro_preprocess_media_library_item__small) and otherwise instantiates Drupal 11.4's ClaroHooks / ClaroFormHooks OOP hook classes and calls the equivalent method. The .module bootstraps by require_once-ing core/themes/claro/claro.theme (or the individual Claro hook-class files) so those functions/classes are available even though Claro is not the active theme. Net effect: core Claro stays the single source of the media-library templates, avoiding a forked copy in the front-end theme that would drift from core on every update. No configuration UI, no permissions, no services. Core requirement ^11.4 is exceptionally tight and pins it to one minor.
